text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, pulling back after a four-day rally that had pushed the stock up nearly $7. The decline came as crude prices softened—U.S. oil dropped to $91.48 per barrel—even as geopolitical tensions remain elevated. News that the U.S. Energy Secretary says an Iran nuclear deal may not happen, combined with ongoing sanctions and military posturing around the Strait of Hormuz, sets a conflicted backdrop: tighter supply and higher risk premiums battle against near-term demand concerns.

The broader oil market is caught between two forces right now. Refinery disruptions in Ukraine and Russia have pushed diesel to record highs and tightened global fuel supply, which normally supports crude prices and integrated producers like ConocoPhillips. But sustained supply uncertainty and talk of possible U.S. intervention in Venezuela's oil sector—a potential wildcard for supply—may have tempered trader appetite for energy stocks today, especially after the stock had run hard in recent days.
